items.statement: Define and control the methods used for decontamination of RABS/isolators (cleaning, bio-decontamination and, where applicable, inactivation of biological materials).
items.quote: Decontamination methods (cleaning and bio-decontamination, and where applicable inactivation for biological materials) should be appropriately defined and controlled.

items.statement: Carry out cleaning before the bio-decontamination step, since leftover residues can reduce decontamination effectiveness.
items.quote: The cleaning process prior to the bio-decontamination step is essential; any residues that remain may inhibit the effectiveness of the decontamination process.

items.statement: Hold evidence showing that the cleaning and bio-decontamination agents do not adversely affect product made inside the RABS or isolator.
items.quote: Evidence should also be available to demonstrate that the cleaning and bio-decontamination agents used do not have adverse impact on the product produced within the RABS or isolator.

items.statement: For isolators, automate, validate and control interior bio-decontamination within defined cycle parameters, and include a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gaseous or vaporised).
items.quote: The bio-decontamination process of the interior should be automated, validated and controlled within defined cycle parameters and should include a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gaseous or vaporized form).

items.statement: For isolators, extend gloves with fingers separated during bio-decontamination so the agent contacts all glove surfaces.
items.quote: Gloves should be appropriately extended with fingers separated to ensure contact with the agent.

items.statement: For isolators, ensure cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination leave the interior surfaces and critical zone free from viable microorganisms.
items.quote: Methods used (cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination) should render the interior surfaces and critical zone of the isolator free from viable microorganisms.

items.statement: For RABS, include routine sporicidal agent application by a validated method shown to reliably reach all interior surfaces and give a suitable aseptic environment.
items.quote: The sporicidal disinfection should include the routine application of a sporicidal agent using a method that has been validated and demonstrated to robustly include all areas of the interior surfaces and ensure a suitable environment for aseptic processing.

items.statement: Qualify cleanrooms and clean air equipment (UDAFs, RABS, isolators) used for sterile manufacture against the required environmental characteristics.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment such as unidirectional airflow units (UDAFs), RABS and isolators, used for the manufacture of sterile products, should be qualified according to the required characteristics of the environment.

items.statement: Provide each manufacturing operation with a suitable environmental cleanliness level in the operational state to minimise contamination risk to product or materials handled.
items.quote: Each manufacturing operation requires an appropriate environmental cleanliness level in the operational state in order to minimize the risk of contamination of the product or materials being handled.

items.statement: Maintain appropriate cleanliness levels in both the at-rest and operational states.
items.quote: Appropriate cleanliness levels in the “at rest” and “operational” states should be maintained.

items.statement: Qualify cleanrooms and clean air equipment using a methodology that meets Annex 15 requirements.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be qualified using methodology in accordance with the requirements of Annex 15.

items.statement: Keep cleanroom qualification (including classification) clearly separate from operational environmental monitoring.
items.quote: Cleanroom qualification (including classification) should be clearly differentiated from operational environmental monitoring.

items.statement: Include in cleanroom and clean air equipment qualification, where relevant to the installation design/operation: filter leakage and integrity testing, airflow volume and velocity, pressure difference, airflow direction and visualisation, microbial airborne and surface contamination, temperature, relative humidity, recovery and containment leak tests.
items.quote: As part of the qualification requirements of Annex 15, the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment should include (where relevant to the design/operation of the installation): i. Installed filter system leakage and integrity testing. ii. Airflow tests - volume and velocity. iii. Air pressure difference test. iv. Airflow direction test and visualisation. v. Microbial airborne and surface contamination. vi. Temperature measurement test. vii. Relative humidity test. viii. Recovery test. ix. Containment leak test.

items.statement: Achieve the Table 1 at-rest particle limits after a clean-up period following completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning.
items.quote: The total particle limits given in Table 1 above for the “at rest” state should be achieved after a “clean up” period on completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning activities.

items.statement: Determine the clean-up period (guidance under 20 minutes) during room qualification, document it and follow it in procedures to restore qualified cleanliness if disrupted during operation.
items.quote: The "clean up" period (guidance value of less than 20 minutes) should be determined during the qualification of the rooms, documented and adhered to in procedures to reinstate a qualified state of cleanliness if disrupted during operation.

items.statement: Justify the unidirectional airflow supply speed in the qualification protocol, including where air speed is measured.
items.quote: The speed of air supplied by unidirectional airflow systems should be clearly justified in the qualification protocol including the location for air speed measurement.

items.statement: Design, measure and maintain air speed so unidirectional airflow protects product and open components at the working position (e.g. high-risk operations, exposed product/components).
items.quote: Air speed should be designed, measured and maintained to ensure that appropriate unidirectional air movement provides protection of the product and open components at the working position (e.g. where high-risk operations occur and where product and/or components are exposed).

items.statement: Ensure unidirectional airflow systems give a homogeneous air speed of 0.36–0.54 m/s (guidance) at the working position, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.quote: Unidirectional airflow systems should provide a homogeneous air speed in a range of 0.36 – 0.54 m/s (guidance value) at the working position, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.

items.statement: Ensure airflow visualisation studies correlate with air speed measurements.
items.quote: Airflow visualization studies should correlate with the air speed measurement.

items.statement: Determine the microbial contamination level of cleanrooms as part of cleanroom qualification.
items.quote: The microbial contamination level of the cleanrooms should be determined as part of the cleanroom qualification.

items.statement: Base the number of microbial sampling locations for qualification on documented risk assessment, classification results, air visualisation studies and process knowledge.
items.quote: The number of sampling locations should be based on a documented risk assessment and the results obtained from room classification, air visualization studies and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Include both at-rest and in-operation states in microbial qualification.
items.quote: Qualification should include both “at rest” and “in operation” states.

items.statement: Grade A qualification microbial limit: no growth for air samples, settle plates and contact plates.
items.quote: A | No growth

items.statement: Grade B qualification microbial limits: air 10 CFU/m3, settle plates (90 mm) 5 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 5 CFU/plate.
Grade C qualification microbial limits: air 100 CFU/m3, settle plates (90 mm) 50 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 25 CFU/plate.
Grade D qualification microbial limits: air 200 CFU/m3, settle plates (90 mm) 100 CFU/4 hours, contact plates (55 mm) 50 CFU/plate.

items.quote: Settle plates should be exposed for the duration of operations and changed as required after a maximum of 4 hours.

items.statement: Base settle plate exposure time on recovery studies and ensure it does not dry out the media.
items.quote: Exposure time should be based on recovery studies and should not allow desiccation of the media used.

items.statement: Use all methods listed in Table 2 for a grade when qualifying an area of that grade.
items.quote: All methods indicated for a specific grade in the table should be used for qualifying the area of that specific grade.

items.statement: Justify the approach if a tabulated method is not used or alternative methods are used.
items.quote: If one of the methods tabulated is not used, or alternative methods are used, the approach taken should be appropriately justified.

items.statement: Where technologies report results other than in CFU, scientifically justify the limits applied and correlate them to CFU where possible.
items.quote: If different or new technologies are used that present results in a manner different from CFU, the manufacturer should scientifically justify the limits applied and where possible correlate them to CFU.

items.statement: Apply the Table 6 contact plate and glove print limits to qualification of personnel gowning.
items.quote: For the qualification of personnel gowning, the limits given for contact plates and glove prints in Table 6 should apply.

items.statement: Ensure sampling methods do not create a contamination risk to manufacturing operations.
items.quote: Sampling methods should not pose a risk of contamination to the manufacturing operations.

items.statement: Visually inspect garments for damage and cleanliness after washing and before packing.
items.quote: After washing and before packing, garments should be visually inspected for damage and visual cleanliness.

items.statement: Evaluate and define garment management processes within the garment qualification programme, including a maximum number of laundry and sterilisation cycles.
items.quote: The garment management processes should be evaluated and determined as part of the garment qualification programme and should include a maximum number of laundry and sterilisation cycles.

items.statement: Keep activities in clean areas that are not critical to production to a minimum, especially during aseptic operations.
items.quote: Activities in clean areas that are not critical to the production processes should be kept to a minimum, especially when aseptic operations are in progress.

items.statement: Ensure personnel move slowly, in a controlled and methodical way, to avoid excessive shedding of particles and organisms.
items.quote: Movement of personnel should be slow, controlled and methodical to avoid excessive shedding of particles and organisms due to over-vigorous activity.

items.statement: Ensure operators doing aseptic operations follow aseptic technique at all times to avoid air current changes that could bring lower-quality air into the critical zone.
items.quote: Operators performing aseptic operations should adhere to aseptic technique at all times to prevent changes in air currents that may introduce air of lower quality into the critical zone.

items.statement: Restrict movement next to the critical zone and avoid obstructing the unidirectional (first air) airflow path.
items.quote: Movement adjacent to the critical zone should be restricted and the obstruction of the path of the unidirectional (first air) airflow should be avoided.

items.statement: Consider including review of airflow visualisation studies in the training programme.
items.quote: A review of airflow visualisation studies should be considered as part of the training programme.

items.statement: For terminally sterilised products, prepare components and materials in at least a grade D cleanroom to limit microbial, endotoxin/pyrogen and particle contamination.
items.quote: Preparation of components and materials should be performed in at least a grade D cleanroom in order to limit the risk of microbial, endotoxin/pyrogen and particle contamination, so that the product is suitable for sterilisation.

items.statement: Where the product is at high or unusual risk of microbial contamination (e.g. supports growth, long hold before filling, not mostly in closed vessels), carry out preparation in at least grade C.
items.quote: Where the product is at a high or unusual risk of microbial contamination (e.g. the product actively supports microbial growth, the product must be held for long periods before filling or the product is not processed mostly in closed vessels), then preparation should be carried out in at least a grade C environment.

items.statement: Prepare ointments, creams, suspensions and emulsions in at least grade C before terminal sterilisation.
items.quote: Preparation of ointments, creams, suspensions and emulsions should be carried out in at least a grade C environment before terminal sterilisation.

items.statement: Clean primary packaging containers and components with validated processes that control particle, endotoxin/pyrogen and bioburden contamination.
items.quote: Primary packaging containers and components should be cleaned using validated processes to ensure that particle, endotoxin/pyrogen and bioburden contamination is appropriately controlled.

items.statement: Fill products for terminal sterilisation in at least a grade C environment.
items.quote: Filling of products for terminal sterilisation should be carried out in at least a grade C environment.

items.statement: Where the CCS shows unusual environmental contamination risk (e.g. slow filling, wide-necked containers, exposure over a few seconds before closing), fill in grade A with at least grade C background.
items.quote: Where the CCS identifies that the product is at an unusual risk of contamination from the environment because, for example, the filling operation is slow, the containers are wide necked or are necessarily exposed for more than a few seconds before closing, then the product should be filled in grade A with at least a grade C background.

items.statement: Where possible, include a microorganism-retaining filtration step in bulk solution processing to reduce bioburden and particles before filling into final containers.
items.quote: Processing of the bulk solution should include a filtration step with a microorganism retaining filter, where possible, to reduce bioburden levels and particles prior to filling into the final product containers

items.statement: Set a maximum permissible time between bulk solution preparation and filling.
items.quote: there should be a maximum permissible time between preparation and filling.

items.quote: A total particle monitoring program should be established to obtain data for assessing potential contamination risks and to ensure the maintenance of the environment for sterile operations in a qualified state.

items.quote: Note 2: The occasional indication of macro particle counts, especially ≥ 5 µm, within grade A may be considered to be false counts due to electronic noise, stray light, coincidence loss etc.

items.statement: Investigate consecutive or regular low-level counts as a possible contamination event.
items.quote: However, consecutive or regular counting of low levels may be indicative of a possible contamination event and should be investigated.

items.statement: In grade A, monitor particles for the full duration of critical processing, including equipment assembly.
items.quote: For grade A, particle monitoring should be undertaken for the full duration of critical processing, including equipment assembly.

items.statement: Monitor grade A continuously for particles ≥0.5 and ≥5 µm with a suitable sample flow rate of at least 28 litres (1 ft³) per minute so all interventions, transient events and system deterioration are captured.
items.quote: The grade A area should be monitored continuously (for particles ≥0.5 and ≥5 µm) and with a suitable sample flow rate (at least 28 litres (1ft³) per minute) so that all interventions, transient events and any system deterioration is captured.

items.statement: Have the monitoring system frequently compare each sample result with alert levels and action limits often enough to identify and respond to excursions in time.
items.quote: The system should frequently correlate each individual sample result with alert levels and action limits at such a frequency that any potential excursion can be identified and responded to in a timely manner.

items.statement: Trigger alarms in grade A when alert levels are exceeded.
items.quote: Alarms should be triggered if alert levels are exceeded.

items.statement: Define in procedures the actions to take in response to alarms, including considering additional microbial monitoring.
items.quote: Procedures should define the actions to be taken in response to alarms including the consideration of additional microbial monitoring.

items.statement: Use a similar continuous particle monitoring system for grade B, although sample frequency may be lower.

items.quote: The grade B area should be monitored at such a frequency and with suitable sample size that the programme captures any increase in levels of contamination and system deterioration.
